call.title: Experiment readout — a one-page checkout lifts conversion
call.content:
Experiment readout — a one-page checkout lifts conversion
better: one-page checkout converted 4.8% vs 4.1% (+0.7 points, 95% +0.2 to +1.2), 41,200 users

## Result
The one-page checkout converted more: 4.8% against 4.1%, and the interval around the difference stays above zero. The test ran 14 days and could have seen a 0.5-point lift, so a result this size is one it was built to find.

## Numbers
| Variant | Users | Converted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| control | 20,540 | 4.1% (842) |
| one_page | 20,660 | 4.8% (992) |
Difference +0.7 points (95% +0.2 to +1.2). Smallest detectable effect at these counts: 0.5 points. Sample ratio 49.9 / 50.1, as designed.

## Caveats
- 14 days covers two weekends but no pay-day week.
- Revenue per order was not in the export; conversion is the only outcome read.

## Decision
Ship the one-page checkout; read revenue per order for two weeks after.

call.title: Experiment readout — a one-page checkout lifts conversion
call.content:
Experiment readout — a one-page checkout lifts conversion
no difference detected: one-page checkout converted 4.4% vs 4.1% (+0.3 points, 95% −0.6 to +1.2), 8,180 users

## Result
No difference detected: the interval around +0.3 points runs from −0.6 to +1.2. With 8,180 users the test could only have seen a lift of 1.3 points or more, so a lift of the 0.5 points hoped for would not show here.

## Numbers
| Variant | Users | Converted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| control | 4,100 | 4.1% (168) |
| one_page | 4,080 | 4.4% (180) |
Difference +0.3 points (95% −0.6 to +1.2). Smallest detectable effect at these counts: 1.3 points. Sample ratio 50.1 / 49.9.

## Caveats
- Underpowered for the hoped-for 0.5 points: it needs about 41,000 users.
- 7 days: one weekend.

## Decision
Keep running until about 41,000 users (roughly 5 more weeks at this traffic), then read again.
